fields.description:
## Context / Problem
The parent-first cascade (`docs/concurrency.md` §I4a) is implemented ONLY in
`transition_compute` / `claim_compute`. The Jira reconciler's inbound-apply path writes
STATUS events **directly**, bypassing that seam entirely:
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py`
(`_inbound_update_write_status_event` and `_inbound_create_write_status_event`) both call
`_write_event_file(tracker_dir, local_id, "STATUS", ...)` with no cascade. So an inbound
Jira status change that moves a child into an active status does NOT pull its ancestors
along, and can compose exactly the invalid states I4a forbids — a `closed` parent holding
an `open`/`in_progress` child.

This is a parity gap on the automated-caller surface, found by the Step-7 parity census
while fixing `paragonite-fruited-minnow` (96db-365e-f2c3-4547).

## Decision (operator ruling)
The operator ruled: "rebar should maintain, as an invariant, that no non-terminal-state
ticket can be a child of a closed ticket." (Recorded verbatim as a comment on this
ticket.) That resolves the open design question: the doc-only option 2 (declare inbound
apply a `cascade=False` surface) is REJECTED; option 1 is chosen — the inbound-reconcile
write surface upholds the same parent-first invariant the interactive cascade upholds.

## Approach
Mirror the interactive cascade at the inbound event-write surface, single-sourced on the
interactive machinery — no second cascade table:

- Add one helper `_cascade_inbound_status_parents(tracker_dir, local_id,
  current_status, target_status)` in `apply_inbound_events.py`. It consults
  `rebar._commands.transition._CASCADING_EDGES` (the one authoritative edge table) and
  `rebar._commands.transition._resolve_parent_in_status` (the one authoritative
  parent-eligibility lookup), and when the child's STATUS edge is a cascading edge with
  an eligible parent, writes the parent's STATUS event FIRST via the same
  `_write_event_file` writer — walking recursively up the chain (topmost eligible
  ancestor first) with a cycle guard, exactly the §I4a ordering.
- Call it from both inbound STATUS writers: `_inbound_update_write_status_event`
  (before the child's STATUS write, using the same `_read_latest_status` previous
  status) and `_inbound_create_write_status_event` (previous status is `open`, so only
  the `open -> in_progress` edge can cascade there). Cascaded parent event paths are
  appended to the update path's `written` list.
- Deliberately do NOT route inbound status through `transition_compute`: inbound apply
  re-materialises peer-recorded state and must stay deterministic and gate-free —
  routing through the interactive verb would subject Jira-originated moves to the
  start-work plan-review gate (an LLM gate) and to eager per-event commit/push,
  breaking the reconciler's batch orchestration. The cascade DECISION (edge table +
  parent eligibility) is shared; only the write primitive differs, matching how the
  inbound path already writes every other event.
- Batch self-consistency / idempotency: suppress the update-path STATUS write when the
  target status equals the current local status (a no-op write). This is what keeps a
  cascaded parent from fighting the parent's OWN inbound status mutation later in the
  same batch (the parent's own write becomes a suppressed no-op), and makes re-applying
  the same inbound payload idempotent. Default: order-independent within a batch —
  whichever of parent/child applies first, the final local state is identical.
- Failure posture mirrors both existing seams: an absent/unreadable/ineligible parent
  yields no cascade and the child proceeds alone (identical to the interactive
  `_resolve_parent_in_status` contract), and a cascade `_write_event_file` failure
  propagates out of the leaf exactly as the child's own STATUS write failure already
  does — no new batch-corruption mode.
- Out of scope (recorded as discovered work if confirmed): the inbound `* -> closed`
  parity with the interactive open-children close guard is a DIFFERENT mechanism (§I4a
  explicitly excludes closing edges from the cascade); this ticket changes only the
  three cascading edges.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py` — the cascade helper +
  calls from the two STATUS writers + the no-op suppression.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — §I4a scoped to BOTH write surfaces (interactive verbs AND
  inbound reconcile), citing the operator ruling.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_status_cascade.py` — new test module
  driving the inbound-apply path (not `transition_compute`).

## Testing
- RED (bypass proof, then GREEN): `_apply_inbound_update` moving a `closed` child to
  `in_progress` under a `closed` parent writes the parent's `closed -> in_progress`
  STATUS event first; reduced states show parent AND child `in_progress` (was: parent
  left `closed` — the I4a-invalid state).
- Chain: grandparent `closed` -> parent `closed` -> child; inbound child reactivation
  cascades both ancestors, topmost first.
- Negative/edge: no parent → no cascade, single STATUS event; parent already active →
  no cascade; `* -> closed` inbound write → never cascades.
- Batch no-fight: after the child's cascade moved the parent, the parent's own inbound
  status mutation to the same status writes NO duplicate STATUS event (suppressed
  no-op).
- Create path: inbound CREATE with status `in_progress` under an `open` local parent
  cascades the parent `open -> in_progress`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A decision is recorded for whether inbound reconcile applies the parent-first
      cascade (operator ruling comment on this ticket; option 1).
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a states explicitly which write surfaces the invariant
      binds (all of them — interactive verbs and inbound reconcile), citing the operator
      ruling; checked by reading the section in the landed change.
- [x] An inbound status change into an active status cascades to eligible ancestors,
      with tests driving the inbound-apply path (not `transition_compute`): the new test
      module above passes, and its central case fails on the pre-fix code (RED
      demonstrated in-session).
- [x] The cascade decision is single-sourced on `_CASCADING_EDGES` /
      `_resolve_parent_in_status` from `rebar._commands.transition` (no duplicated edge
      table); checked by inspection of the diff.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the complexity ratchet, and the targeted reconcile
      test suites (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`) pass in the worktree.
